clue.text: Refined charisma, a thing of the past

indicators.note: something refined has been processed and reworked, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of this word are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone laments that polished charm has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an old word or custom kept on after its time, a relic from earlier days.

clue.text: A posh couple’s help

blocks.note: taken as written
U means upper-class, the language of the posh
a couple is two of something

explanation.surface: A wealthy couple has a domestic helper.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British label for posh speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign person living with a family and helping with childcare and housework.

clue.text: Short, extremely seemly gesture

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: curt means brief or short in manner
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A brief, very proper bow or bob.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a respectful movement of bending the knees, a polite bodily sign made to royalty or a dance partner.

clue.text: A mountain range, a mountain range

blocks.note: taken as written
the Pennines are the hill range running down northern England

explanation.surface: A geography quiz answer that just repeats the question.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition looks like a typo; the first half is the definition and the second half splits into a plus the English range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the chain of peaks running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Decent type with soft heart, health for the most part failing

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped
something failing breaks down, so the combined letters collapse into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person whose health is in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from the Sermon on the Mount, describes a thoroughly good, honest, unpretentious person.

clue.text: With weapon? Not I packing heat

indicators.note: the instruction says the letter I must be left out of the preceding word
to pack something is to stuff it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are armed replies that they are not carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packing heat' is slang for carrying a gun, which hides that heat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is a moderate degree of heat, the two words being close synonyms.

clue.text: Old-fashioned stove favoured once more

blocks.note: an Aga is a traditional British range cooker
in means fashionable or in favour

explanation.surface: A traditional cooker comes back into favour.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron cooking range common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, repeated, a direct adverb synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Mania on vacation: '1,000 insects! Enormous creatures!'

blocks.note: the word with its middle emptied
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
moths are winged insects

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker panics at a swarm of a thousand bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoths were huge extinct elephant-like beasts, and the word is also used for anything gigantic.

clue.text: Think twice about abandoning cultivated aesthetic

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a piece is taken away
cultivated ground is turned over and worked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: c, for circa, means about, and this is the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders before ditching a refined artistic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'think twice about' but is the letter C that has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause before acting out of doubt, much like reconsidering a decision.

clue.text: Fabulous officer in range set out to discharge gunshot

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to pepper is to spray with shot from a gun

explanation.surface: An officer on a firing range lines up to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means fictional, the stuff of fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sgt Pepper is the invented bandleader of the Beatles album, a made-up military rank holder.

clue.text: Composer with practically modest, humble dwelling

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word falls one letter short

blocks.note: pure in the sense of chaste or modest, then cut short
a cell is a small bare room, as for a monk

explanation.surface: A composer lives in a nearly plain, simple home.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was the leading English Baroque musician, writer of Dido and Aeneas.

clue.text: Rejecting queen, marquess turns philosopher

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so a letter is removed
turning things around jumbles them, so the remaining letters change order

blocks.note: Q is the chess abbreviation for queen, and the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist scholar and thinker.

clue.text: Ad-libs entrance, getting around playwright

indicators.note: the words wrap around the target, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An actor improvises on stage while making an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist behind A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Section of cathedral undergoing renovation for a long time

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Part of a cathedral has been covered in scaffolding for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ loft is the raised gallery in a church or cathedral where the pipe organ stands.

clue.text: Australia hadn't thrown Test; England missing bowler – perhaps? End of story!

missing means lacking, so one letter is left out of the previous word

blocks.note: A is the international vehicle code for Australia
taken as written
taken as written

a bowler is a kind of hat; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides that bowler means a hat; a Test is an international cricket match.

clue.text: Scare about European Union suppressing retrograde imperial weight: blimey

blocks.note: taken as written
the usual abbreviation
lb is the abbreviation for a pound, an imperial weight

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era headline: Europe bans the old pound weight, causing a scare.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French, which suits the European surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacré bleu is a stereotypical French exclamation of surprise, matching the English interjection of astonishment.

clue.text: Awkwardly struggle with fish

blocks.note: first meaning: to move or act clumsily and with difficulty
second meaning: a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily wrestles a fish they have caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stagger or thrash about helplessly, and the noun names a flat sea creature such as plaice.

clue.text: Take case from Edam before getting crackers and cheese

crackers is informal for mad

explanation.walkthrough: Crackers and Edam pull toward a cheese course; crackers means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is the Swiss cheese with large holes, a pale firm variety from the Emme valley.

clue.text: ... but a stem cell could become salad ingredient

indicators.note: the letters could be turned into something else by changing their order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

clue.text: Asian city where movie villain returns to get minerals

clue.text: Tory PM’s barren lands

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath led a British Conservative government; the apostrophe is the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaths are open areas of poor soil covered with heather and gorse, unsuitable for farming.

clue.text: Take advantage of past boyfriend when something goes bad

clue.text: Stay up to let in eastern poet

clue.text: Get rid of quiet, accommodating Republican

blocks.note: ease is calm, quiet rest

clue.text: Belittle English in German leaflet

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.walkthrough: Horny is used literally: the male has horns.

clue.text: Enjoy a condiment

blocks.note: first meaning: to take great pleasure in
second meaning: a pickle or chutney served with food

clue.text: Pants with pockets
